answer: Con la evidencia disponible, el recurso mas cercano es 'Impact of Tight Lats and Pectorals on Posture and Spine': When the pectorals and latissimus dorsi are too short and overactive, they pull the shoulders forward, round the upper spine, and can push the lower spine into extension (hyper-lordosis). This creates a shortened and compressed spinal position and restricts rib cage expansion. Ejercicios relacionados encontrados: Quadruped Scapular Protraction Breathing Drill, Optimized Seated Face Pull Technique.
key_points: When the pectorals and latissimus dorsi are too short and overactive, they pull the shoulders forward, round the upper spine, and can push the lower spine into extension (hyper-lordosis). This creates a shortened and compressed spinal position and restricts rib cage expansion.

Attempting to correct posture by squeezing the shoulders back and standing excessively tall compromises several biomechanical aspects, including proper breathing mechanics, natural spinal curvature, and healthy shoulder movement.
A breathing and movement drill performed in a quadruped position to create space between the scapula and spine, thereby improving shoulder external rotation mobility.

To effectively target the upper back and improve posture, perform face pulls seated with external stability (e.g., a bench). This allows for a focus on proper scapular protraction and retraction, leading with the elbows, without compensatory spinal movements.
cautions: Actively squeezing shoulders back to 'stand tall'
Avoid shrugging your shoulders during the drill.
Do not force the movement or breathing.
